records.name: Ollama
records.plain: A tool for running AI models on your own machines or through a hosted plan.
records.description: Ollama makes it easy to download and serve AI models. On the mesh it appears two ways: as a cloud plan (the fast path for live chat) and as a local server (the always-works backup). The routing rules decide which one answers.

records.name: vLLM
records.plain: High-throughput AI serving: 120-160 requests per second with fast first words.
records.description: vLLM is the production serving engine for AI models. It batches many requests at once and manages memory smartly. On the mesh it turns the desktop's graphics chip into a shared answering server for the whole network.

records.name: LiteLLM
records.plain: A traffic controller that sits in front of many AI models.
records.description: LiteLLM gives every caller one address and handles the switching behind it: if a provider fails or runs dry, the next one takes over automatically. It runs in its own service box (CT 123).

records.name: HyperFrames
records.plain: Turns web pages into finished videos.
records.description: HyperFrames renders HTML and CSS animations into MP4 files, which means video becomes code: reviewable, versioned, and re-renderable. It is the render engine behind the Field Reports and the section headers.

records.name: Manim
records.plain: The animation engine behind famous math explainer videos.
records.description: Manim draws precise mathematical and diagram animations. On the mesh it is the engine of choice when a shot is about a formula, a system, or a process that benefits from exact drawing.

records.name: Remotion
records.plain: Builds videos with React, the popular web-app tool.
records.description: Remotion lets programmers make videos with the same framework they build web apps with. Scenes are components, so they can be tested like software.

records.name: Motion Canvas
records.plain: A programmer's sketchpad for technical animation.
records.description: Motion Canvas is for technical storytelling: it animates ideas with code-first precision. It rounds out the four-engine video landscape as the sketch-first option.

records.name: FFmpeg
records.plain: The free media converter that stitches, converts, and processes audio and video.
records.description: FFmpeg is the plumbing of the media pipeline: it joins rendered scenes with voice tracks, converts formats, and handles every file conversion. It is free, scriptable, and everywhere.

records.name: Opus Clip
records.plain: Cuts long videos into short vertical clips automatically.
records.description: Opus Clip takes a finished video and produces short vertical versions for social media. In the pipeline it is the repurposing step: one render becomes many posts.

records.name: WebGPU
records.plain: A modern way for web pages to use your graphics chip.
records.description: WebGPU gives the browser a fast path to the GPU. It is what makes speech-to-text run entirely in the browser on your own machine, which is why Glassy's transcription never uploads audio.

records.name: Whisper
records.plain: An open speech-to-text model that runs locally.
records.description: Whisper transcribes voice to text. Running it in the browser on your own graphics chip means the recording never leaves the machine - the privacy promise holds end to end.

records.name: ElevenLabs
records.plain: A service that generates realistic AI voices.
records.description: ElevenLabs creates the narrated voice tracks for videos. The production brief marks its use honestly: if a synthetic voice is used, the video says so.

records.name: yutu
records.plain: A tool that lets AI assistants manage a YouTube channel.
records.description: yutu gives agents the ability to upload, update, and organize videos through the official YouTube API. It is the upload step of the video pipeline.

records.name: Rive
records.plain: A tool for interactive, lightweight animations.
records.description: Rive makes small, crisp animations that run anywhere. On the mesh it is one of the motion tools an AI assistant can drive through its MCP connection.

records.name: LottieFiles
records.plain: A library of real animation craft and lightweight web animations.
records.description: LottieFiles contributes the motion-design skill layer: real patterns from shipped products, plus the Lottie format for lightweight animations.

records.name: Impeccable
records.plain: An open-source skill that lists 46 classic AI design mistakes to avoid.
records.description: Impeccable codifies the generic-AI defaults - the overused font, the purple gradient, the card inside a card - as detectors. It keeps AI-designed pages from looking AI-designed.

records.name: OpenClaw
records.plain: An open platform with 210,000+ stars and 5,700+ shared agent skills.
records.description: OpenClaw is a large open ecosystem for running AI agents. On the mesh it runs alongside Hermes, and its shared skill library is one of the reasons the stack grows so fast.

records.name: Hermes
records.plain: The AI agent platform that anchors the mesh - always on, always scheduled.
records.description: Hermes is the always-on agent runtime: its gateway is the scheduler, its memory is disciplined, and its helpers run the boring parts of the day. It is the brain the fleet talks to.

records.name: Glassy
records.plain: A calm, local-first note-taking app designed for easily-overwhelmed brains.
records.description: Glassy keeps notes in one file you own, runs speech-to-text in your own browser, and follows strict design rules: high contrast, calm motion, two typefaces. Privacy is its architecture.

records.name: OpenMontage
records.plain: The first open-source video studio run by an AI agent.
records.description: OpenMontage puts the AI agent in charge of decisions and gives it Python tools and memory. Governance is the product: cost tracking, locked runtimes, and pre-render checks keep quality from collapsing.

records.name: Mission Control
records.plain: The operations floor: one dashboard that shows every service at a glance.
records.description: Mission Control gathers the task board, scheduled jobs, notes, and nine other services into one page with fixed rules. It is where the humans look first when something changes.

records.name: Pulse
records.plain: The fleet health monitor: watches every machine and powers the health panels.
records.description: Pulse checks hosts and services around the clock and feeds the health tiles on Mission Control. Green means nothing happened - the best news an operations floor can deliver.

records.name: Gitea
records.plain: A self-hosted code server - your own private GitHub.
records.description: Gitea stores the mesh's code repositories on home hardware. Version control stays local-first, with the same workflows as any big platform.

records.name: n8n
records.plain: A visual automation builder - drag-and-drop workflows between services.
records.description: n8n connects services with visual workflows. It is one of the automation options the mesh surveys (and one of the tools marked 'do not use' in the decisive creator-stack review, in favor of script-first automation).

records.name: Tailscale
records.plain: A private network that connects your devices over the internet, encrypted.
records.description: Tailscale gives every machine a stable private address and connects them as if they shared one Wi-Fi. It is how the desktop reaches the server from anywhere.

records.name: WireGuard
records.plain: A fast, modern VPN technology - the backup network path.
records.description: WireGuard is the backup way for devices to reach each other when the main private network path fails. The mesh keeps it configured and tested.

records.name: Proxmox
records.plain: Free software that splits one big computer into many small, isolated ones.
records.description: Proxmox hosts the service boxes: 26 small containers, about 15 running at all times. Each one is isolated, so a broken service does not take its neighbors down.

records.name: NATS
records.plain: A lightweight message bus that carries events between services.
records.description: NATS is the mesh's nervous system for events: when something happens in one service, NATS carries the news to the listeners that care - like the activity feed on the dashboard.

records.name: Honcho
records.plain: A long-term memory service for AI agents.
records.description: Honcho stores cross-session context so agents remember between conversations. It runs on its own container and is one of the three memory layers.

records.name: MCP
records.plain: Model Context Protocol - a standard plug-in system that lets AI agents connect to tools.
records.description: MCP is how agents discover and use tools: search, voice, automation, and more. The mesh runs 21 of these plug-in connections, and the planned Mesh Directory becomes one too.

records.name: Git
records.plain: Version control: every change saved with a date, a message, and a way back.
records.description: Git is why nothing on the mesh is ever truly lost. Rules, decisions, and content are versioned like code - and a disaster-recovery skill exists for the day something goes wrong.

records.name: GitHub
records.plain: The public home for open-source code - where this site's source now lives.
records.description: GitHub hosts the EricPoziverse repository: the site, its tools, and its documentation, public and open-licensed.

records.name: Playwright
records.plain: A browser automation tool - drives real browsers for tests, screenshots, and video.
records.description: Playwright drives real browsers. On the mesh it records footage, verifies deployments, and captures the evidence screenshots behind the receipts.

records.name: React
records.plain: The popular web-app framework - used to build testable video components.
records.description: React builds interfaces as components. In the video stack, Remotion uses React to build video scenes that can be tested like software.

records.name: Anthropic Claude
records.plain: One of the AI model families in the routing pool.
records.description: Claude models appear in the mesh's routing plans as strong general models. Model choice always follows verified benchmark data, not marketing.

records.name: MiniMax M3
records.plain: The fast reasoning model that powers the mesh's main agent brain.
records.description: MiniMax M3 is the model behind the primary agent profile: deep reasoning at the operator's side, with its own provider account so scheduled jobs never eat the chat allowance.

records.name: DeepSeek
records.plain: An AI model family used in the mesh's research and harness work.
records.description: DeepSeek models appear in the mesh's model research - the benchmark tables and the harness experiments that decide which model gets which job.

records.name: LangGraph
records.plain: The framework behind the coding team: a supervisor, a builder, and a reviewer.
records.description: LangGraph runs the coding pipeline as a real supervisor loop - up to five iterations and three replans, then a human review. Every handoff is saved to a shared checklist.

records.name: Chrome DevTools Protocol
records.plain: The remote-control protocol for browsers - how agents drive and verify pages.
records.description: CDP lets programs drive a real browser: click, read, screenshot, record. The mesh uses it for deployment verification and for capturing b-roll footage.

records.name: VS Code
records.plain: The code editor - where humans and agents meet over the same files.
records.description: VS Code is the shared editor: the operator writes and reviews, and agents propose changes to the same versioned files.
